Organic chemistry connects the shapes of molecules to what they do. In this
course you will draw structures, explain reactions, and use experimental
evidence to decide whether a chemical explanation holds up.

This five-week teaching route is designed for the new **7.5-credit Organic
Chemistry 1 (5KE231)** in the Life Science programme. Use your course's official
instructions for dates, laboratory arrangements and assessment requirements.

::: {.course-start}
**Start with a molecule and a question.**

Open [Reading organic structures](structures/lec.qmd), then work through its
[practice](structures/exercise.qmd) and [self-check](structures/quiz.qmd).
Keep paper or a structure-drawing tool beside you.
:::

## Your route through the chemistry

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .course-card}
### Week 1 · Read and explain

[Structures](structures/exercise.qmd), [properties and IR](properties/exercise.qmd),
and [acids and bases](acids-bases/exercise.qmd).

Read the atoms and bonds, explain a physical property, and predict where a proton moves.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .course-card}
### Week 2 · Think in three dimensions

[Conformations](conformations/exercise.qmd), [stereochemistry](stereochemistry/exercise.qmd),
and [electron flow](mechanisms/exercise.qmd).

Distinguish a rotated view from a different stereoisomer and draw a defensible mechanism.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .course-card}
### Week 3 · Predict a transformation

[Substitution](substitution/exercise.qmd), [elimination and addition](elimination-addition/exercise.qmd),
and [alcohols and redox](alcohols-redox/exercise.qmd).

Use a small reaction toolkit and explain competing pathways.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .course-card}
### Week 4 · Understand carbonyl chemistry

[Carbonyl addition](carbonyl-addition/exercise.qmd), [acyl chemistry](acyl-chemistry/exercise.qmd),
and [amines and aromatics](amines-aromatics/exercise.qmd).

Follow the shared mechanistic patterns that will reappear in biochemistry.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .course-card}
### Week 5 · Decide from evidence

[Spectroscopy](spectroscopy/exercise.qmd), [synthesis and evidence](synthesis-evidence/exercise.qmd),
and [integration](integration/exercise.qmd).

Combine structures, reactions, spectra and calculations into a justified conclusion.
:::
:::

## R belongs beside the laboratory notebook

Use R for calculations, tables and plots, and R Markdown to keep methods,
results and interpretation together. The chemistry still needs your drawing
and explanation. You will calculate amounts and yield, plot an ionisation
model, and present TLC and spectral evidence.

- [Download the student project](downloads/organic-chemistry-student.zip).
- [Restart R and Knit your first report](intro/r-restart.qmd).
- [Find data dictionaries and exercise files](reference/data.qmd).
- [Use the chemistry reference toolkit](reference/toolkit.qmd).
- [Find paper chemistry problems for every study day](practice/index.qmd).
- [Explore the interactive demo for each study day](demos/index.qmd).

## How to use a day

Choose a week and day in the left menu. Its lecture, Exercises, self-check
and demo are grouped together. Review days link back to the relevant lectures.

Study the slides, pause to draw and predict, then solve the exercises
before opening their hints and worked checks. Finish with the self-check.
Return to earlier representations and electron-flow rules whenever a reaction
seems like an isolated fact to memorise.
